title: Minimal propositional logic and the role of explosion

based_on.title: Proofs and Types (web reprint 2003, corrected 1990 edition)

summary: Remove explosion from natural deduction, separate contradiction from arbitrary conclusions, and compare minimal, intuitionistic and classical proof rules.
abstract: A proof of a contradiction normally allows us to conclude anything. What remains of deduction if we remove that rule? Minimal logic keeps the introduction and elimination rules for the connectives, including the rules that produce a contradiction, while allowing that contradiction to remain unresolved. We prove that familiar negation laws survive, recover intuitionistic logic by adjoining exactly the explosion schema, and use ordered models that allow a contradiction to remain true to show why disjunctive syllogism can fail. The comparison also separates two classical principles: double-negation elimination restores explosion, whereas excluded middle alone does not.
